harness.scene: The area is a 3D scan of a real alpine river valley: a stone footbridge over a rocky river, stone paths, trees and steep banks, open to the sky. An altitude geofence a few metres above the ground acts like a roof, so the drone cannot climb over tall obstacles.

licence.detail: CC BY 4.0, matching the owner metadata retrieved 2026-11-20 from https://superspl.at/scene/fb6b9fae.

attribution.detail: "Verzasca River - Ponte dei Salti, Switzerland" by tosolini (https://superspl.at/scene/fb6b9fae), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

scale.detail: Not measured. Recorded so far: Scene units treated as metres at scale 1, without independent calibration. (Shown for information; not enforced.)

passage.detail: Narrowest gap on the flight graph: 0.93 m (the drone is 0.50 m wide) at [-28.6, -0.8, -25.3].

alignment.detail: 97.4% of 4282 sampled surface cells of the scan's own collider (the altitude fence and sealed hollows excluded) have scan points within 0.70 m (needs 90%).

coverage.detail: 98.9% of 185 waypoints have captured scan ground below them (needs 90%). Captured means at least 133 scan points within 2 m (5% of this scan's median, 2657). 2 waypoints sit over ground with no scan surface within 2.5 m (ground we sealed).

scene-text.detail: The area is a 3D scan of a real alpine river valley: a stone footbridge over a rocky river, stone paths, trees and steep banks, open to the sky. An altitude geofence a few metres above the ground acts like a roof, so the drone cannot climb over tall obstacles.

routes.detail: 108 routes (12 train, 24 dev, 24 heldout, 48 test) match sim/scenarios/reach-verzasca-valley.json.

between.detail: Reactive avoider 33.3%, between straight 8.3% and planner 100%.

missions-search.detail: Sets match sim/scenarios/mission-verzasca-valley-search.json. Each target used once. Oracle completed 4 of 4 development missions.

targets-captured.detail: 84 of 84 targets have at least 133 scan points within 2 m (5% of this scan's median, 2657).

targets-sky.detail: 84 of 84 targets are in their column's topmost free space.
